content.title: About
content.content: Red cabbage is a leafy vegetable from the Brassica oleracea var. capitata f. rubra cultivar. It has a vivid purple‑red color, crisp texture, and a mildly sweet‑to‑bitter flavor. Raw red cabbage is commonly used in salads, sauerkraut, and as a side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The deep color comes from anthocyanins, powerful antioxidants.
Red cabbage belongs to the cruciferous family, along with broccoli, cauliflower, and Brussels sprouts.
Raw leaves retain more vitamins than cooked ones.
It can be fermented to make kvass or other probiotic drinks.
Historically, cabbage symbolized abundance and health in many cultures.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Red cabbage provides over 100 mg of vitamin C per 100 g, supporting immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and other polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: High fiber content promotes healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains potassium, calcium, and magnesium, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Cruciferous vegetables can cause increased gas in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Thyroid considerations
items.content: Goitrogens may affect iodine absorption; people with thyroid issues should consume in moderation.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cabbage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the cabbage thinly for salads, use it as a base for sauerkraut, roll it fresh with other vegetables, or serve it as a crunchy side. Lightly marinating in vinegar and salt can soften the texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a perforated bag. Properly kept, it stays fresh for 2‑3 weeks. Remove any wilted leaves to prevent spoilage.

content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑sodium cheddar is an aged cow’s‑milk cheese with the salt level cut to about 0.5 % compared with regular cheddar. It retains the sharp, slightly nutty flavor and firm, crystalline texture, but contains less sodium, making it a better choice for low‑salt diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheddar originated in the English county of Somerset in the 12th century.
The lower sodium level is achieved by using less salt during curd formation and special starter cultures.
The cheese is aged 6–12 months, giving it a more pronounced flavor than younger varieties.
Reduced‑sodium cheddar is popular among people managing hypertension.
Cheddar melts well, making it a favorite for casseroles, sauces, and grilled dishes.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Cheddar provides a good source of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A serving supplies about 25 % of the daily protein requirement for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cheddar contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for nervous system function and energy metabolism.

items.title: Reduced sodium
items.content: The lower salt content helps control blood pressure for those monitoring sodium intake.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: During aging, beneficial bacteria develop, supporting gut health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheddar still contains lactose, which can cause discomfort for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein may react to cheddar.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Cheese is energy‑dense; portion control is important for weight management.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Cheddar contains saturated fats, so those with high cholesterol should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reduced‑sodium cheddar works well sliced for sandwiches, grated over salads, melted in casseroles, sauces, or fondue, and as a snack on its own. Let the cheese sit at room temperature for about 30 minutes before serving for a milder flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cheese in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2–4 °C. For longer storage (over 2 weeks), wrap it in wax paper to prevent drying out. Do not keep at room temperature for more than 4 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Grilled flounder is a delicate white fish with a mild flavor, cooked on a grill. Grilling preserves its natural taste, giving a slightly crisp exterior while keeping the flesh juicy. Flounder is rich in protein, omega‑3 fatty acids, and B‑group vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Flounder is a flatfish that lives in coastal waters and rivers, capable of changing its skin color for camouflage.
In cuisine it is often cooked whole, but fillets are popular for their tender texture.
Grilling imparts a smoky aroma that enhances the fish’s natural flavor.
Flounder is considered a delicacy in many Asian and European cuisines.
Compared to many other fish, flounder contains low levels of mercury, making it safe for regular consumption.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Flounder provides complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support heart health and help reduce inflammation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: B12, B6, and niacin aid nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Flounder supplies selenium, phosphorus, and magnesium, important for bones and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Unlike fattier fish, grilled flounder remains relatively low‑calorie.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including flounder.

items.title: Overcooking
items.content: Excessive grilling can create harmful compounds such as acrylamide.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the fish is marinated or served with sauces, sodium levels may be high.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Grilled flounder can be served as a main dish with vegetables, potatoes, or rice. Fillets are easy to slice for salads, sandwiches, or appetizers. A squeeze of lemon, fresh herbs, and a light seasoning highlight its flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked grilled flounder in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a tightly sealed bag for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Vegetarian Gravy is a thick, aromatic sauce made from vegetable broth, plant-based fats, and spices. It is designed to accompany potatoes, vegetables, vegetarian patties and other dishes as a plant‑based alternative to traditional meat gravy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vegetarian gravy is often based on mushroom broth, which gives it a characteristic "meaty" flavor.
There are many variations: with soy sauce, tomato paste, smoked spices, etc.
The sauce keeps well in the refrigerator for up to 7 days and can be frozen for up to 3 months.
While classic recipes use flour for thickening, vegetarian versions frequently use corn starch or tapioca.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Contains protein from soy or pea ingredients, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Plant oils such as rapeseed oil provide mostly polyunsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides vitamin B6 and niacin, which aid metabolic processes.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Herbs and spices like rosemary and thyme have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the vegetable broth helps maintain normal gastrointestinal function.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: If the gravy contains soy protein, individuals with soy allergy may experience reactions.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared gravy can be salty; people monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional thickener is wheat flour; choose a gluten‑free version if needed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the gravy gently to a light simmer and pour over mashed potatoes, roasted vegetables, vegetarian patties or burgers. It can also be stirred into stews for a richer consistency.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size containers for up to 3 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: NFS High-Protein Drink is a ready‑to‑drink shake with high protein content, low calories, and a light texture. It is designed to support muscle recovery after workouts and is convenient to use anytime.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink provides 30 g of protein per serving from whey and plant sources.
It includes B‑vitamins and minerals such as calcium and magnesium to support energy metabolism.
The product is gluten‑free, lactose‑free, and contains no artificial sweeteners.
Packaging is made from recyclable material and is fully recyclable.
Each bottle is a single‑serve, making it ideal for travel and sports activities.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Protein promotes muscle growth and repair, supporting protein synthesis after exertion.

items.title: Low calorie count
items.content: A modest calorie load helps maintain energy balance during an active lifestyle.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C and zinc contribute to a strengthened immune system.

items.title: Enhanced recovery
items.content: Fast‑absorbing amino acids accelerate recovery after intense training.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Electrolytes in the drink help maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Whey protein may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with dairy intolerance.

items.title: Excessive protein intake
items.content: Too much protein can strain the kidneys, especially in people predisposed to kidney issues.

items.title: Artificial sweetener content
items.content: Some versions may contain sucralose or stevia, which are not suitable for everyone.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: High calcium levels can affect the absorption of certain antibiotics and alkaline drugs.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Consume one ready‑to‑drink shake (250 ml) immediately after training or as a snack between meals. For extra flavor, add fresh berries or a banana.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the drink in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, refrigerate and consume within 24 hours.

pizza-with-meat-and-fruit-thick-crust.title: Pizza with meat and fruit, thick crust

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with meat and fruit is an original combination of juicy meats (such as ham, sausage or beef) and sweet fruits (pineapple, mango, peach) on a thick, crunchy crust. The pizza balances salty, sweet and aromatic flavors for a vivid culinary experience.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The meat‑and‑fruit pairing is popular in Hawaiian cuisine, where the classic “Hawaiian” pizza features ham and pineapple.
A thick crust holds more sauce and toppings, making each slice richer.
Fruits add vitamin C and help balance the saltiness of the meat.
These pizzas are typically baked at 220‑250 °C for 12‑15 minutes.
Some regions caramelize the fruit to enhance sweetness.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Fruits contribute vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium, while meat adds iron and zinc.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: The dough and cheese deliver complex carbs and fats, offering sustained energy.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Using whole‑grain flour in the crust increases fiber, supporting digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Fruits contain antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Thick crust, cheese, and meat make the pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Processed meats and sauces can be high in salt, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger reactions in people allergic to lactose or casein.

items.title: Fruit sugar
items.content: Sweet fruits raise blood sugar, important for individuals with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the pizza into serving pieces and serve hot. Garnish with fresh basil or arugula for extra aroma. Optionally sprinkle oregano, black pepper or chili flakes for added spice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore crust crispness.

content.title: About
content.content: Potato home fries are diced or sliced potato pieces that are partially boiled and pre‑fried, then packaged in single‑serve bags. The product is ready to heat in a microwave or on a skillet, delivering a crisp exterior with a tender interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Home fries are usually made from high‑starch potato varieties, which give them a crunchy crust.
The product is frozen for convenient storage and retains its quality for up to 12 months.
Minimal oil is used during processing, making it less fatty than traditional pan‑fried potatoes.
Potatoes are one of the world’s most consumed vegetables, and home fries are popular in the US and Europe as a quick side dish.
When properly reheated in a microwave, up to 80 % of vitamin C is retained, compared with significant loss during prolonged cooking.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potatoes provide a good amount of potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B6 and niacin, important for metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: When no salt is added, the product is suitable for low‑sodium diets.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Potatoes contain carotenoids and flavonoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Acrylamide content
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potential toxin. The frozen product is processed under controlled conditions, but overheating should be avoided.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes can raise blood sugar quickly, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Added salt
items.content: Some versions contain added salt; choose the unsalted option if you need to limit sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the bag in the microwave (3‑4 minutes) or pan‑fry until golden brown. Serve as a side to meat, fish, or enjoy as a snack, seasoned with fresh herbs, spices, or your favorite sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product in a freezer at –18 °C. After opening, consume within 3‑4 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

content.title: About
content.content: Apple strudel is a classic Central European dessert consisting of thin, flaky pastry wrapped around a filling of fresh apples, sugar, cinnamon, and raisins. The pastry is crisp, while the filling is juicy and aromatic.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The strudel originated in Austria in the 18th century and quickly spread across Europe.
Traditionally the dough is rolled so thin that you can see the hand through it.
Apple strudel is often dusted with powdered sugar and served with a butter sauce or vanilla ice cream.
The original recipe uses only one egg and no leavening agents.
There are many filling variations: besides apples, people use cherries, cheese, or nuts.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Apples provide a good amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Apple fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in apples help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Regular apple consumption is linked to lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium contributes to normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Wheat/gluten allergy
items.content: The pastry contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The sweet apple filling adds calories; individuals with diabetes should watch portion size.

items.title: Butter content
items.content: The dough is often brushed with melted butter, increasing saturated fat levels.

items.title: Burn risk
items.content: Hot strudel can cause mouth and throat burns, especially in children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the strudel warm, sliced into portions. It can be dusted with powdered sugar, drizzled with a butter sauce, or accompanied by a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the strudel to room temperature, then store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months.
